title: New accounts are seeded from the organisation
description:
Design only for now (see HUM-be87f4 comments): a service-managed StackSet on an OU delivers the baseline; accounts are created as code in a small org repo; read-only everyday SSO with a break-glass admin. Built last, after Ryan decides.

```gherkin
Feature: New accounts arrive seeded

  Scenario: A new account in the Papyrus deployments OU gets the baseline
    Given an account created in the Papyrus deployments OU
    When it joins the OU
    Then the organisation delivers the baseline stack automatically
    And the account's pipeline can deploy without a person touching it
```

comments.author: home
comments.text:
# Design: new accounts are seeded from the organisation

For accounts inside the DataParade AWS Organization: an account is declared in an organisation repo; a pipeline creates it; the organisation delivers the baseline. Design only; no organisation change is made.

## 1. Creating the account: two options
| | `AWS::Organizations::Account` via CloudFormation | Control Tower Account Factory |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fit | Same deployer, same Git-then-pipeline flow | Needs a landing zone with extra Log Archive and Audit accounts |
| Cost | Free | The service is free but enables Config and CloudTrail, which cost (verify) |
| Risk | Deleting the resource removes the account from the organisation: use `DeletionPolicy: Retain` | More moving parts |
Recommendation: CloudFormation; no Control Tower. The account email is a person's address and never goes in Git: it comes from an SSM String parameter in the management account that a person creates. The default account quota may be small (raising it is a support request by a person; verify). Enable centralized root access management so member accounts carry no root credentials (verify availability).

## 2. Seeding with a StackSet
- The OU "Papyrus deployments" is an `AWS::Organizations::OrganizationalUnit`. The baseline is a service-managed `AWS::CloudFormation::StackSet`, staged rollout (`FailureToleranceCount: 0`, low `MaxConcurrentCount`).
- The baseline needs per-account parameters (repo, prefix, budget name, `GithubSubjectPrefix`), so a bare auto-deployed instance would fail. Recommended: `StackInstancesGroup` entries in the same stack as the account declare each account with `ParameterOverrides`, so adding an account is one merge. Auto-deployment can be enabled later if the baseline accepts an empty repo as a no-op (small template change). `GithubSubjectPrefix` comes from `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/oidc/customization/sub`, written into `accounts.json`; the repo must exist first. Verify that overrides are accepted alongside auto-deployment.
- Conflict to resolve: a StackSet-owned stack cannot be modified from inside the account, and it is not named `<prefix>-github-deploy`. For seeded accounts the organisation owns the baseline: the `roles-apply` role, the `cloudformation-roles` service role and the `pipeline-roles` environment are not needed. This needs a baseline switch (for example `ManagedByOrganisation`) and a workflow input that skips the baseline apply. Benefit: one merge changes the baseline for the whole fleet.

## 3. The management account
- A new `org-pipeline` stack holds the GitHub OIDC provider, deploy/plan/roles-apply roles and a CloudFormation service role limited to Organizations, StackSet and Identity Center APIs, denying `LeaveOrganization`, `DeleteOrganization`, `CloseAccount`. It is the one hand-made apply (a single documented command, like the account baseline).
- Honest limit: "narrow" means a narrow API surface. Whoever merges a StackSet template change can deliver any IAM change to every seeded account. Controls: main-only trust, branch protection, `allowed-changes.json`, CloudTrail alerts, SCPs.
- The org repo can be public (no email or account id in it), so GitHub Actions and OIDC apply. A private repo would need CodeBuild. Later option: a delegated administrator for StackSets.

## 4. Access with IAM Identity Center (management account)
| Permission set | Use | Session |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Everyday-ReadOnly` | People and agents, with data-read denies | 8 hours |
| `BreakGlass-Admin` | Named admins only | 1 hour |
Both are defined in CloudFormation with their assignments. Break-glass alerting: an EventBridge rule on sign-in events for the `AWSReservedSSO_BreakGlass*` role to SNS, address from SSM (verify region, event name `AssumeRoleWithSAML`, and whether an organisation trail is needed; a first management-events trail is free, extra copies and storage cost). Person-only: enabling Identity Center, creating users and groups, MFA settings, assigning people.

## 5. SCP guardrails worth having (on the OU, never on the management account)
Deny leaving the organisation; IAM users and access keys; disabling CloudTrail; the root user; regions outside an allowed list (use `NotAction` for global services: IAM, Route 53, CloudFront, ACM in us-east-1); edits to `*-github-*` roles and the baseline stack except by the pipeline and break-glass principals (test: it could break the IMPORT flow). SCPs are small (5,120 characters).

## 6. One-time setup (an administrator of the management account)
1. Confirm all features are enabled. 2. Enable trusted access for CloudFormation StackSets. 3. Enable Identity Center (optionally centralized root access). 4. Create the SSM parameters for account emails and the alert address. 5. Apply `org-pipeline` once with the documented command. 6. Set the repo variable for the management account id. 7. Merge: the pipeline creates the OU, SCPs, accounts, StackSet and permission sets. 8. In Identity Center create people and assign permission sets.

## 7. Cost
Organizations, SCPs, StackSets, Identity Center and IAM roles are free. Cost budgets without actions are free (action-enabled budgets beyond the free two cost a few cents a day: verify). A Route 53 zone is about 0.50 USD a month. Amplify, AppSync, Lambda and storage are per usage. Control Tower is not used.

## 8. Risks and what is not built
Risks: the management account is the highest-trust place; StackSet changes touch every account at once; account quota and root-credential removal are unverified. Not built: the `org-pipeline` template, the org repo, the baseline switch, permission sets, the alert rule, SCPs, auto-deployment on a no-op baseline, the CodeBuild variant.
